title: The last note
text:
Raka held his angklung so tightly that his knuckles turned white. In the school hall, two hundred chairs were filling up with parents, grandparents and wriggling little brothers and sisters.

Each child in Class 4 had one angklung, and each angklung played just one note. Together, they would play a whole song. Raka's note came at the very end. If he missed it, the song would have no ending at all.

“Just watch my hand,” Bu Sari, their teacher, had said at every practice. “When I point to you, shake.”

The curtain opened. The lights were hot and bright. Raka could see Nenek, his grandmother, in the front row, waving a small paper fan.

The song began. The notes bounced around the hall like rain on a tin roof. Raka counted the beats under his breath, but halfway through, a baby started to cry and he lost his place. His mouth went dry. Was it the third line or the fourth? He stared at his music, but the dots swam in front of his eyes.

Then he noticed Mei, standing next to him. She was tapping her foot, very gently, in time with the music. Tap, tap, tap. Raka tapped his foot too. Slowly, the song began to make sense again. He could hear the tune climbing towards the end.

Bu Sari turned. Her hand pointed straight at him.

Raka shook his angklung. The last note rang out, clear and round, and floated up to the ceiling.

For a moment, the hall was silent. Then everyone burst into applause. Nenek was on her feet, clapping with her fan still in her hand.

Raka let out a long breath and grinned at Mei. “Thank you,” he whispered.
